_readme: Word classes: one meaning, every spelling this market uses for it.
Person-independent, which is why it sits in sources/ beside professions.json. It is
NOT a second copy of the keyword tables - it is the define-once layer above them: a
class names a meaning, and the words in it are the spellings a posting may use. The
intended wiring is to widen the tables that already exist at load time (load_vocab's
keywords, the profile's tags, and the weighted fit/score tables), so a synonym
inherits the weight of whichever word of the class is already in that table, and no
table gains a meaning it did not already have.
THIS FILE IS THE SCORE, since 2026-09-22. A posting is labelled with every class
it names (`skills` on the corpus row), and both numbers a profile puts against a
class - expertise and importance - are paid out over those labels: 90 points split
evenly over what one posting asks for. The `title` and `professions` axes are read
separately, to widen a profile's target titles into every other name for that job.
axis  - which vocabulary the class is meant to widen: professions, domains, tags,
title (a job-title alias, which is a different thing from a word synonym),
or one of the five skill sections:
managerial - leading people and delivery: agile, project management,
governance, mentorship, hiring, culture, OKRs.
personal   - traits and how you work with others: proactive, curious,
communication, negotiation, stakeholder management.
knowledge  - Industry Knowledge (LinkedIn's name): a concept, pattern,
field or regulation tied to no one product - system design,
DDD, monorepo, microservices, CI/CD, GMP, MDR, payments.
technical  - what you write or perform hands-on: languages, frameworks,
protocols (REST, GraphQL), lab techniques (PCR, HPLC).
tooling    - a branded product you log into, install or operate:
Datadog, Jira, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, SAP.
A skill class sits in exactly one section. It may be a
LIST when one meaning widens two vocabularies, which is how a class avoids
being written twice.
about   - one plain sentence on what the skill means, shown when hovering it. Only where
the label alone is ambiguous (Platform, Governance, Swift); optional.
caution - where the class is known to over-reach. A class with a caution must never be
expanded outside its axis.
except - phrases that hold one of the class's words and mean something else
("post-marketing" for marketing, "not screened by artificial intelligence" for ai).
Blanked out of the posting before this class alone is tried.
criticality - how much doing a job depends on the skill, 1-10. The 90 skill points of
both scores are split in proportion to it. Omitted, the section decides:
technical 10, tooling 8, knowledge 6, managerial 4, personal 2 (CRITICALITY
in app/server/fetch/profile.ts). Set it where the section is wrong for a class.
Translations live in the same flat `words` list as the synonyms, in English, Spanish,
German and French. Matching is lowercase over the posting's own text, so the language of a
spelling changes nothing about what it matches and a second level of nesting would
buy a label nobody reads. A short word is left OUT rather than guarded: the cautions
record which ones and why.
A trait (personal) is matched over the whole posting body, where employers describe
themselves too - so its words are candidate-describing phrases ('sense of
responsibility', 'innovative mindset'), never the bare adjective ('responsible',
'innovative'), and each class records in `caution` what it still over-reaches into.
Matching (profile.ts buildSkills, normalise.ts detectSkills): every token of a word of 5+
letters takes German/English endings, a 3-4 letter acronym a plural s (KPIs), a -y word
-ies; a trailing * is a stem. German suspended compounds ("Kommunikations- und
Koordinationsfähigkeit") and lists in front of a head noun ("communication and
presentation skills") are spelled out first, and the sections a posting spends on the
employer (About us, Wir bieten, Benefits...) are dropped (text.ts dropOfferSections).
Umlaut plurals (abschlüsse) and glued compounds (stakeholdermanagement) are NOT derived:
list them. 2026-09-30: 107 classes added from an audit of 90 postings over 18 professions.
A class's FIRST word is its skill name in the CV prompt (cv.ts skillNames): keep it the plain
English name a CV would use ("microsoft office", not "vba"). Round 2 the same day: 32 more
classes and 41 renamed first words after 72 fresh postings and 36 sample CVs were checked.

classes.label: Engineer / developer
classes.caution: Software only. 'Process engineer', 'Verfahrensingenieur' and the footwear/polymer engineers On (Zurich) posts match these words and are exactly what filters.non_software drops.

classes.label: AI / machine learning
classes.caution: Bare 'ai' needs a word boundary or it fires inside 'chain' and 'maintain' - the reason it was missing from domains.software-it and briefly hid the Novartis Applied AI role.
except: without the use of artificial intelligence

classes.label: Agents / agentic systems
classes.caution: 'agent' alone is not in this class: insurance agent, service agent, agent-based modelling. Only the qualified spellings are safe. Bare 'assistant' was office/executive assistants: 57% support-admin.

classes.label: Retrieval-augmented generation
classes.caution: Singular 'embedding' is 'embedding Celonis as a strategic platform', not vector embeddings.

classes.label: Frontend / client-side
classes.caution: Not bare 'browser': every cookie banner names it.

classes.label: Platform / developer experience
classes.about: Building the internal platform and tooling other engineers work on (developer experience, IT infrastructure) - not a product platform.
except: enables organizations to increase developer productivity

classes.label: Leading people
classes.caution: 'lead' on its own also means 'lead engineer' (no reports) and, in German, 'Leitung' of anything. Leadership is asked-for, not proven, by any of these.

classes.label: Client-facing engineering (title alias)
classes.caution: A title alias, not a synonym: these are the same job under different employer vocabulary. A plain 'consultant' or 'client advisor' is not in this class - that is sales or private banking.

classes.label: Preclinical / non-clinical study work
classes.about: Study work before human trials: safety, efficacy and toxicology in lab and animal models.

classes.label: Translational research
classes.about: Moving research from the lab into first-in-human and proof-of-concept studies.

classes.label: Quality & regulatory
classes.caution: Bare 'qa' also means test automation in software, and 'audit' means financial audit in a bank. Life-science axis only.

classes.label: Leading a project or programme
classes.caution: 'Study director' and 'principal investigator' are science-lead titles and stay out of this class: they lead the science, not the programme.

classes.label: React
classes.caution: 'react' is a normal English verb - it needs a word boundary and, next to a framework list, still matches 'reacts to incidents'.

classes.label: Modular UI architecture
classes.about: Splitting a frontend into independent parts: component architecture, micro-frontends.

classes.label: LLM application development
classes.caution: The `llm` class names the model; this one names building on top of it. A posting that only mentions the noun is not evidence of this skill.

classes.label: AI-assisted development
classes.about: Coding with an AI assistant at your side: GitHub Copilot, Cursor, AI pair programming.
classes.caution: Not bare 'copilot': Microsoft 365 Copilot is an office product an admin rolls out.

classes.label: Agentic coding workflows
classes.about: Working with autonomous coding agents that write and change code on their own.

classes.label: Context engineering
classes.about: Deciding what an LLM sees in its context window: retrieval, prompt context, memory.

classes.label: Machine learning
classes.caution: Bare 'ml' is deliberately absent - unanchored it matches 'html'. The `ai` class carries these words too; that one tags a posting, this one is a skill somebody has or has not.

classes.label: Python
classes.caution: 'py' alone is too short to match safely and is left out.

classes.label: Node.js
classes.caution: Bare 'node' is not in this class: a cluster node, an edge node and a lymph node all match it.

classes.label: Systems integration
classes.about: Connecting enterprise systems through middleware, interfaces and integration platforms (iPaaS).

classes.label: CI/CD
classes.caution: 'build pipeline' is sales prospecting: 89% of 108 hits were account executives.

classes.label: Game development
classes.caution: Candidate-asking phrases only: a studio's boilerplate says 'games' and 'players' on every posting, HR included, so bare 'game', 'games' and 'game studio' are left out. Criticality 9, not knowledge's 6: a studio asking for shipped games is asking for the domain itself.

classes.label: Game engines (Unity / Unreal)
classes.caution: Bare 'unity' is left out: 'team unity' and Unity the company's HR postings.

classes.label: Feature flags (LaunchDarkly / Flagsmith)
classes.about: Switching features on and off in production without a deploy.
classes.caution: Bare 'feature flag' and 'unleash' are left out: the first names a practice, not a tool, and 'unleash your potential' is recruiting boilerplate.

classes.label: Observability
classes.about: Seeing what running software does: logging, metrics, tracing, APM, OpenTelemetry.
classes.caution: German 'Überwachung' is patient or process monitoring in hospitals and plants, not software observability. Not bare 'monitoring': condition, risk and compliance monitoring are other jobs.

classes.label: Authentication and identity
classes.about: Login and permissions: IAM, SSO, OAuth / OIDC.

classes.label: SQL databases
classes.about: Relational databases and the SQL language.
classes.caution: The product names are spellings of the skill, not tooling rows: nobody advertises 'postgres' meaning anything but SQL work.

classes.label: Test automation
classes.about: Automated tests that run without a human: unit, integration, end-to-end.

classes.label: Product analytics
classes.about: Measuring how users use a product: event tracking, funnels.

classes.label: Nx
classes.about: Nx, a build system and toolkit for JavaScript / TypeScript monorepos.
classes.caution: Two letters: only safe with a word boundary, and it still collides with the chemical and part-number senses of 'nx'.

classes.label: AWS
classes.caution: 'lambda' is deliberately absent - the maths and the Greek letter outnumber the service.

classes.label: GitHub
classes.caution: 'gh' alone is too short and is left out.

classes.label: ERP systems
classes.about: Enterprise resource planning systems that run finance, supply chain and operations.

classes.label: CRM systems
classes.about: Customer relationship systems such as Salesforce or HubSpot.

classes.label: SAP FICO
classes.caution: Bare 'fico' is left out: in a US posting it is a credit score.

classes.label: IDoc
classes.about: SAP's IDoc format for exchanging documents between systems.

classes.label: SAP Smart Forms
classes.about: SAP's tool for designing printed forms.

classes.label: IPTV set-top platforms
classes.about: TV delivered over IP networks and its set-top boxes.
classes.caution: 'stb' is left out - three letters, and it is a gene name and a stock ticker too.

classes.label: Engineering management
classes.caution: 'em' is left out - two letters, and it is an em-dash, an electron microscope and a unit of width. Bare 'development manager' is business/sales development: 75% commercial.

classes.label: Line management
classes.about: Having direct reports: people leadership, team lead.

classes.label: Platform strategy
classes.about: Owning a technology strategy and roadmap.

classes.label: Setting engineering standards
classes.about: Setting the coding standards and guidelines a team follows.

classes.label: Driving technology adoption
classes.about: Leading change: rolling out new technology, digital transformation, enablement.

classes.label: Hiring and technical assessment
classes.caution: 'recruiter' and 'recruiting' are deliberately absent: they are what filters.non_eng drops, and a posting for a recruiter is not evidence of this skill. Bare 'hiring' went the same way - 'we are hiring' is on every posting there is. 'Our talent acquisition team can help...' is interview-process boilerplate on 395 postings, not a hiring skill. German 'Einstellung' is mostly attitude ('positive Einstellung') or machine setting, not hiring.

classes.label: Cross-functional collaboration
classes.about: Working across teams and disciplines.

classes.label: Engineering culture
classes.caution: 'dx' is left out - two letters, and in a life-science corpus it is 'diagnosis'.

classes.label: Agile delivery
classes.caution: 'safe' the scaling framework is left out: the English adjective is everywhere in a job posting.
except: in einem agilen und innovativen umfeld

classes.label: Governance
classes.about: Compliance and governance: following rules and regulations, audit readiness, GRC, SOX.

classes.label: Rust
classes.caution: 'rust' is also corrosion - a real word in a manufacturing or materials posting.

classes.label: Go
classes.about: The Go programming language.
classes.caution: Bare 'go' is left out: word-bounded it still matches 'go to market' in every second posting.

classes.label: Java
classes.caution: The closing boundary is what keeps this off 'javascript'. Without it every JS posting is a Java posting.

classes.label: Swift
classes.about: Apple's Swift programming language - not the SWIFT banking network.
classes.caution: Bare 'swift' is left out twice over: the English adjective, and SWIFT the interbank network - which in this registry of Swiss banks is the likelier meaning.

classes.label: Next.js
classes.caution: 'SSR' is also SRG SSR, the Swiss broadcaster - 67% of its hits were that employer.

classes.label: Web platform
classes.about: The browser platform itself: HTML, web components, browser APIs, PWA, WebAssembly.

classes.label: Google Cloud
classes.caution: 'gcp' is left out on purpose - in a life-science posting it is Good Clinical Practice, and this registry carries both kinds of employer.

classes.label: DevOps / SRE
classes.about: Running software in production and the culture around it: DevOps, SRE, platform engineering.

classes.label: Caching
classes.about: Keeping data in fast storage close to where it is needed, to avoid recomputing or refetching it.

classes.label: Business intelligence
classes.about: Dashboard and reporting tools: Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Qlik.

classes.label: Data protection
classes.caution: Not bare 'datenschutz': the privacy footer of every Swiss careers page. The compounds name the work.

classes.label: Blockchain and digital assets
classes.caution: Bare 'custody' is ordinary bank custody at Pictet and every private bank.

classes.label: Design tools
classes.about: UI design tools: Figma, Sketch, Adobe XD.

classes.label: Project tracking tools
classes.about: Project tracking tools: Jira, Confluence, Asana, MS Project.

classes.label: Presenting
classes.caution: English 'moderation' is content moderation (trust & safety), not facilitation.

classes.label: Technical writing
classes.caution: Bare 'documentation' is left out: measured on live postings it fired on 6 of 15, because every engineering job asks for documented work. Only the phrases that name the skill are kept.

classes.label: FDA submissions
classes.caution: Bare 'ind' also fired inside 'indépendant' and 'indústria' (a boundary bug, fixed) and on the 'Ind.' abbreviation.

classes.label: Design control
classes.about: The regulated medical-device design process: design history file, verification and validation.

classes.label: In vivo models
classes.about: In vivo research with animal (often rodent) models; FELASA training.

classes.label: Immunoassays
classes.about: Antibody-based lab tests: ELISA, Western blot, lateral flow.

classes.label: Molecular biology
classes.caution: Bare 'sequencing' is mostly 'sequencing of work' in PM, sales and finance postings.

classes.label: Technology transfer
classes.about: Scaling a process up and transferring it into production (industrialisation) - not university tech licensing.
classes.caution: Bare 'scale-up' is company stage ('a fast-growing scale-up'), not process scale-up. Generic Spanish 'scaling'. Generic German 'scaling'.

classes.label: Sales
classes.caution: This is what filters.non_eng drops from a title. It is here as a SKILL so a posting that wants it shows a grey chip - not so a sales job reaches an engineer's list.

classes.label: Training and enablement
classes.about: Training people and passing on knowledge.
classes.caution: Bare 'training' is out: half its matches here were 'pre-training' and 'training and serving frontier AI models', which is model-training, not teaching people. Only the phrases that mean a taught programme are kept.

classes.label: Process improvement
classes.caution: 'lean' earns its place on 'lean methodologies' but will also catch 'lean team' and 'lean into'. Watch it if the chip starts appearing everywhere. Bare 'lean' is 'lean team' boilerplate - one employer's 'lean autonomous teams' was 60% of hits.

classes.label: Manufacturing
classes.caution: Bare 'manufacturing' does fire on an employer's own description of itself ('one of two global manufacturing bases'). Kept anyway - a posting at a manufacturer plausibly involves it - but it is the weakest word in here.

classes.label: Financial analysis
classes.caution: Bare 'forecasting' is mostly sales pipeline forecasting: 53% commercial.

classes.label: Reporting and KPIs
classes.about: Producing management, financial or regulatory reports, dashboards and KPIs.
classes.caution: Bare 'reporting' is out: 'reporting to the Head of X' and 'reporting into Operations' are org-chart sentences on a large share of postings, not a skill.

classes.label: Networking
classes.about: Computer networks: TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls, VPN, load balancers - not professional networking.
classes.caution: Bare 'networking' is as often professional networking ('in-house networking' on every Datadog posting).

classes.label: Process automation
classes.about: Automating business workflows: RPA, workflow tools, intelligent automation - not factory automation (see Industrial automation).

classes.label: Electronics
classes.caution: 0% of these postings hit any class before this one existed.

classes.label: Robotics
classes.caution: 0% before this class - 7 employers were talking about robots into silence.

classes.label: CAD
classes.caution: 'creo' and 'inventor' are out: both are CAD products and both are ordinary words - 'creo' is Spanish for 'I believe', and this file carries Spanish.

classes.label: Natural language processing
classes.caution: Absent from the snippets, which are 400 characters of company blurb - not evidence it is absent from the postings.

classes.label: Knowledge graphs
classes.about: Modelling knowledge as linked entities and relations, often to ground AI systems.

classes.label: Quality assurance
classes.about: Making sure a product or process meets its standard - in software or in regulated manufacturing.
classes.caution: 'qa' and 'qc' are two letters and are kept only because they are near-universal in this exact spelling in a job posting; they still need the word boundary.

classes.label: Stability and shelf life
classes.about: Testing how long a product stays within spec (shelf life).

classes.label: Human factors and usability
classes.about: Usability engineering for medical devices (IEC 62366) and use-related risk.

classes.label: Post-market surveillance
classes.about: Watching a device or drug after launch: vigilance reporting, PMCF, clinical evaluation reports.

classes.label: Assay development
classes.about: Designing and validating a lab test that measures something reliably.

classes.label: Formulation and drug delivery
classes.caution: 0% before this class.

classes.label: Biosafety
classes.caution: 'Biological safety' is left out - in medtech it means the ISO 10993 biological safety evaluation, which is the biocompatibility class. Bare 'bsl' is left out too.

classes.label: Statistics software
classes.about: Statistics packages: SPSS, SAS, Stata, GraphPad Prism, Minitab.

classes.label: Office and collaboration tools
classes.caution: Bare 'excel' is out. It reads clean on the 400-character snippets and would not on the body, where 'candidates who excel at' is boilerplate - the fetch matches the whole posting, so the snippet is the weaker test.

classes.label: Backend
classes.caution: The subject, not the stack: a Java class already exists and says which language. 'Back office' is a different thing entirely and does not match - the boundary after 'back' is what stops it.

classes.label: Mobile
classes.caution: 'Mobile' alone also appears in 'mobile workforce' and 'mobility solutions'; the second does not match, the first does. Kept because a mobile-app posting says the bare word more often than any phrase. Bare 'mobile' is mobile phones, mobile robotics, 'mobile-abos' - facilities was 13% of hits.

classes.label: Event-driven architecture
classes.about: Systems that communicate through events and message queues instead of direct calls.

classes.label: Full-text search
classes.about: Search over text: indexing, ranking, relevance.

classes.label: Proactive / takes initiative
classes.caution: 'Proactive monitoring' and 'proactive maintenance' are duties, not a trait - accepted, since the word still asks for the same behaviour.

classes.label: Autonomy / self-starter
classes.caution: 'autonomie' is also battery life or a vehicle's range in a French medtech or automotive posting.

classes.label: Innovative / creative thinking
classes.caution: Bare 'innovative' and 'innovation' are left out on purpose - every employer calls itself innovative, and that asks nothing of the candidate.

classes.label: Passionate / driven
classes.caution: Company boilerplate ('we are passionate about...', 'mit Leidenschaft') is why bare 'passion' is left out; 'leidenschaftlich' still reaches into company text.

classes.label: Responsive / reacts quickly
classes.about: Reacting quickly when something comes in.
classes.caution: Bare 'responsive' is responsive web design and is left out; 'responsiveness' can still be a UI performance word in a frontend posting.

classes.label: Ownership / sense of responsibility
classes.about: Taking responsibility for an outcome without being told to.
classes.caution: Bare 'responsible' is left out - 'you will be responsible for' opens half the duties lists in the corpus.

classes.label: Efficient / structured way of working
classes.about: A structured, efficient way of working.
classes.caution: Bare 'efficient' is left out - 'efficient processes' describes the employer's systems, not the candidate.

classes.label: Communication
classes.caution: Bare 'communication' is left out - communication systems, internal communications and the corporate-comms department ask nothing of a candidate's manner.

classes.label: Teamwork
words: work as part of a team
working as part of a team

classes.label: Adaptability
classes.caution: Bare 'flexibility' is left out - it is flexible hours in most postings. 'adaptable' can still describe a product.

classes.label: Resilience / works under pressure
classes.caution: Bare 'resilience' and 'resilient' are system properties in an engineering posting and are left out.

classes.label: Analytical thinking
classes.caution: Bare 'analytical' is analytical chemistry and analytical methods in a lab posting.

classes.label: Team advocacy / psychological safety
classes.about: Protecting the team: psychological safety, servant leadership.

classes.label: OKRs / goal setting
classes.about: Setting goals and measuring them with OKRs.

classes.label: Performance management
classes.caution: 'Application performance management' contains 'performance management' - an APM tooling posting will fire it.

classes.label: Delivery / release management
classes.about: Planning and running releases.

classes.label: API contracts / contract testing
classes.about: Agreeing an API's shape up front and testing against it: contract-first, consumer-driven contracts, Pact.

classes.label: Matomo
classes.about: Matomo, an open-source web analytics tool.

classes.label: Strapi

classes.label: Contentful
classes.about: Contentful, a hosted headless CMS.

classes.label: Kong API gateway

classes.caution: Bare 'kong' is left out - it matches 'Hong Kong'.

classes.label: Vercel / Netlify
classes.about: Hosting platforms for web frontends: Vercel, Netlify.

classes.label: German (language)
classes.caution: Never bare 'deutsch' or 'german': every Swiss page carries a language switcher, and 'German-speaking Switzerland' is a region, not a requirement.

classes.label: English (language)
classes.caution: Never bare 'english': half the corpus is written in it. A requirement is a phrase.

classes.label: French (language)
classes.caution: Never bare 'français' or 'french': the switcher on every Swiss page.

classes.label: Italian (language)
classes.caution: Never bare 'italiano' or 'italian': the switcher on every Swiss page.

classes.label: Consulting / advisory
classes.about: Advising clients as a consultant (management or IT consulting) - not a consulting firm as employer.
classes.caution: Not bare 'consulting' or 'beratung': one is half the employer names on a board, the other is the health and careers advice every benefits section offers.

classes.label: IT service management (ITSM / ITIL)
except: sla (service level agreement) bei der abholung

classes.label: Low-code platforms
classes.about: Building apps with little code: Power Apps, OutSystems, Mendix, Appian, Retool.

classes.label: Chatbots / conversational AI

classes.label: Data governance / data quality

classes.label: Industrial automation (PLC / SPS)

classes.label: Maintenance / servicing

classes.label: Commissioning / qualification

classes.label: Virtualisation

classes.label: Cardiology / cardiovascular

classes.label: Neurology / neuroscience

classes.label: Orthopaedics / bone / spine

classes.label: Radiology / medical imaging
